messages:
maya: Seeing increased gRPC retries crossing rack boundaries, started ~09:13 UTC. P50 latency up ~30ms, packet loss ~1.6% on internal LB flows.
sam: Which LB? internal-ml-inference-lb?
jin: Yes, hostpool spans rack-a and rack-b. Symptoms: session stickiness dropped during handoffs.
maya: quick tail of the proxy logs shows 'upstream connection reset by peer' on sessions that cross ToR. Local rack traffic stable.
ash: quick healthcheck — can we dump ethtool + MTU on a few hosts? Doing on host inf-ml-03...
ops-bot: alert: interface errors rising on inf-ml-03 (ifOutErrors).
sam: ethtool shows MTU=9000 on inf-ml-03, but neighbor inf-ml-26 reports MTU=1500. Suspect MTU mismatch between racks/ToRs.
jin: That would explain fragmentation and drops for RDMA-backed flows (we use SRoCE on these nodes).
maya: running `ip -s link show dev ens3f0` and `rdma link show` now. Output: RX errors spiking, but link still up.
ash: grabbed ToR configs: tor-rack-a uplink MTU=9000, tor-rack-b uplink MTU=1500. Looks like a template drift on rack-b.
sam: How did tor-rack-b get 1500? Any recent net-config rollouts? @net-eng?
deploy-bot: net-config-rollout tor-rack-b completed 1778998000
jin: If the rollout applied a default template it could've reset MTU. For RDMA, MTU mismatch is deadly.
maya: mitigation idea: force LB to prefer local pool (session affinity zone-local) for 30m to avoid cross-rack paths while net-eng fixes MTU.
ash: Doing temporary affinity change on internal-ml-inference-lb -> sessions pinned to local rack pools. :thumbsup:
sam: Also consider enabling ECN on ToRs so congestion is signaled instead of dropped, but primary fix is MTU normalization.
ops-bot: monitoring: internal-ml-inference-lb p50 latency dropping back to baseline after affinity change.
jin: Plan: 1) Confirm all ToR uplink MTUs and normalize to 9000 2) Re-run RDMA bringup on affected nodes after fix 3) Audit net-config templates and rollback the offending patch if found 4) Add MTU assertion to net CI
maya: opened ticket NETENG-452 with screenshots, diffs, and affected host list, pinged @net-eng on-call.
ash: Post-incident note: add a rack-level MTU monitoring alert and a preflight check in the rollout pipeline to catch template drift.
sam: For tracking - adding short postmortem stub to the incident board. Will update once net-eng confirms remediation.
maya: thanks folks, I'll keep the affinity pinned for 30m and watch for any RDMA tears.
